witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 76.7a
div.ab: Reddantur uero patri uel filio uel fratri uel qui propinquior est de patre, si predictos parentes non habeat; si omnes istos habeat, et ipsi diuidant inter se.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 593 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: die Wittwe, der schon Leis Wl 9 einen Halsfang-Antheil zuweisen, fehlt; also meint Brunner (Zeitschr. f. Rechtsg. III 16), hier liege früheres Angelsächs. Recht vor
the widow, to whom Leis Wl 9 already assign a share of the halsfang, is missing; Brunner (Zeitschr. f. Rechtsg. III 16) therefore thinks that earlier Anglo-Saxon law is found here

div.ab: And let them be paid to the father or the son or the brother, or to whoever is nearest on the father's side, if he does not have the aforesaid kinsmen; if he has all these, let them divide it among themselves.
